A system is characterized by the following state equation and output equation (\(u\): input, \(\mathbf{x}\): state vector, \(y\): output)
\[\dot{\mathbf{x}} = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ -a & 0 \end{bmatrix}\mathbf{x} + \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}u\]
\[y = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\mathbf{x}\]

\[y = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\mathbf{x}\]

question_text:
Consider an \(n \times n\) orthogonal matrix \(A\) with real entries and each column having unit Euclidean norm.
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.text: The value of the determinant of \(A\) is either +1 or –1

\(\|A\boldsymbol{x}\| = \|\boldsymbol{x}\|\), for all \(\boldsymbol{x} \in R^n\), where \(\|\boldsymbol{x}\|\) denotes the Euclidean norm of \(\boldsymbol{x}\), and \((A\boldsymbol{x})^T(A\boldsymbol{y}) \ne \boldsymbol{x}^T\boldsymbol{y}\), for all distinct \(\boldsymbol{x}, \boldsymbol{y} \in R^n\)

\(\|A\boldsymbol{x}\| = \|\boldsymbol{x}\|\), for all \(\boldsymbol{x} \in R^n\), where \(\|\boldsymbol{x}\|\) denotes the Euclidean norm of \(\boldsymbol{x}\), and \((A\boldsymbol{x})^T(A\boldsymbol{y}) = \boldsymbol{x}^T\boldsymbol{y}\), for all \(\boldsymbol{x}, \boldsymbol{y} \in R^n\)

question_text: Consider the system of linear equations: \(Ax = b\), where \(A\) is an \(n \times n\) matrix, and \(x\) and \(b\) are \(n\)-dimensional column vectors. Suppose this system of equations has a unique solution. Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.text: The system of equations \(A^m x = b\) also has a unique solution for \(m = 1, 2, 3, \ldots\)
\(\text{rank}(A) < \text{rank}([A \mid b])\), where \([A \mid b]\) denotes the augmented matrix.
